subject.title: bug(cost): mid-session writes to bootstrap-injected files trigger cacheWrite spiral on long agentic sessions; bootstrap-cache.ts shipped for #43532 is content-equality, not session-freeze

question: Should OpenClaw support volatile bootstrap files through a dynamic cache-boundary config, an explicit session-freeze mode, or documented opt-in mitigations only?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent answer creates a prompt-cache/config contract and may change whether long-lived sessions see live bootstrap-file edits automatically.

options.title: Adopt dynamic-file contract
options.body: Add a narrow `bootstrapDynamicFiles` or equivalent context contract aligned with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/65438 so volatile files can move below the cache boundary without freezing all bootstrap context.

options.title: Add session-freeze mode
options.body: Introduce an explicit session-stable bootstrap snapshot mode that keeps system-prompt copies frozen while file tools continue to read live disk state.

options.title: Document opt-in mitigations only
options.body: Keep current live-refresh defaults and document `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`, smaller `MEMORY.md`, and cache-boundary caveats as the supported operator path.

recommendation.title: Adopt dynamic-file contract
recommendation.body: Add a narrow `bootstrapDynamicFiles` or equivalent context contract aligned with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/65438 so volatile files can move below the cache boundary without freezing all bootstrap context.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the related bootstrap snapshot cache and is the best available owner for deciding whether the original session-freeze expectation should become a supported product contract.
